items.title: Examining the role of information integration in the continued influence effect using an event segmentation approach

judge.evidence_topic: Misinformation regarding the cause of an event often continues to influence an individual's event-related reasoning, even after they have received a retraction.
judge.evidence_empirical: Experiments 1 and 2 employed spatial event segmentation boundaries in an attempt to manipulate the ease with which a retraction can be integrated into a participant's mental event model.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) utilizando cenários de eventos fictícios, cumprindo o critério de neutralidade. O estudo é empírico, composto por dois experimentos, e o achado principal relatado está devidamente sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: Executive function and the continued influence of misinformation: A latent-variable analysis

judge.evidence_topic: Misinformation can continue to influence reasoning after correction; this is known as the continued influence effect (CIE). The current study investigated whether individual differences in EF could predict individual differences in CIE susceptibility.
judge.evidence_empirical: Participants completed several measures of EF subcomponents, including those of updating and inhibition, as well as set shifting, and a standard CIE task.
judge.reason: O artigo descreve um estudo empírico com participantes humanos utilizando uma tarefa padrão de CIE (neutra) e medidas de função executiva, confirmando a metodologia e o achado principal relatados.

items.title: The inhibitory impact of collaboration on the continued influence effect of misinformation

judge.evidence_topic: The continued influence effect (CIE) of misinformation refers to the persistence of misinformation's impact on memory and inference even when individuals are aware of a retraction.
judge.evidence_empirical: This study examined whether collaborative processes affect the CIE and investigated the underlying mechanisms through three experiments.
judge.reason: O artigo trata do efeito de influência continuada (CIE) através de experimentos empíricos com participantes humanos. O método descrito nos dados extraídos é consistente com o resumo, e o achado principal sobre a colaboração por turnos atenuar o CIE é diretamente sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: Did he or didn't he? Mixed evidence for the continued influence of retracted misinformation on person impressions

judge.evidence_topic: Here we report three experiments that tested for the continued influence of retracted misinformation on person impressions... Participants formed an impression of a fictitious person based on a series of behaviour statements.
judge.evidence_empirical: Here we report three experiments that tested for the continued influence of retracted misinformation on person impressions
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico (três experimentos) sobre o efeito de influência continuada com materiais neutros (pessoa fictícia), atendendo aos critérios. O tamanho da amostra não consta no resumo, e o achado principal reflete exatamente o que está escrito no texto.

items.title: Does Mud Really Stick? No Evidence for Continued Influence of Misinformation on Newly Formed Person Impressions

judge.evidence_topic: Across four experiments, we investigated the impact of person-related misinformation and its correction on dynamic (moment-to-moment) impression formation. Participants formed an impression of a protagonist, “John”, based on a series of behaviour descriptions, including misinformation that was later retracted.
judge.evidence_empirical: Across four experiments, we investigated the impact of person-related misinformation and its correction on dynamic (moment-to-moment) impression formation.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) usando um cenário fictício neutro (impressão sobre um personagem 'John'), o que atende aos critérios. O método descrito no resumo condiz com o que foi extraído. O tamanho da amostra não está presente no resumo, conforme indicado. O achado principal é sustentado pelo texto do resumo.

items.title: Exploring factors that mitigate the continued influence of misinformation

judge.evidence_topic: Across three studies, we evaluated the relative contribution of three factors (i.e., targeting the misinformation, providing an alternative explanation, and relative importance of the misinformation content) to the reduction of the CIE.
judge.evidence_empirical: Across three studies and two different CIE measures, we found that alternative provision consistently resulted in CIE reduction.
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico (três experimentos) sobre o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) utilizando materiais neutros, conforme solicitado. O achado principal está diretamente sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: The role of discomfort in the continued influence effect of misinformation

judge.evidence_topic: Research examining the continued influence effect (CIE) of misinformation has reliably found that belief in misinformation persists even after the misinformation has been retracted.
judge.evidence_empirical: The present research tested the prediction that retractions of misinformation produce feelings of psychological discomfort... Studies 1 and 2 found that retractions of misinformation elicit psychological discomfort... Study 3 showed that the relations between discomfort and continued belief in and use of misinformation are causal in nature
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico (3 experimentos) sobre o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) utilizando cenários neutros (conforme padrão da literatura de CIE, como o incêndio em armazém mencionado nos dados extraídos). O achado principal está diretamente sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: Effective mitigation of the belief perseverance bias after the retraction of misinformation: Awareness training and counter-speech

judge.evidence_topic: This paper contributes to research on mitigating the belief perseverance bias after the retraction of misinformation by proposing counter-speech and awareness-training techniques and comparing them in terms of effectiveness to the existing counter-explanation technique in an experiment with N = 251 participants.
judge.evidence_empirical: in an experiment with N = 251 participants.
judge.reason: O artigo descreve um experimento com 251 participantes para testar técnicas de mitigação do viés de perseverança da crença após a retratação de desinformação, o que se alinha ao pedido. O achado principal sobre a eficácia da técnica de contra-argumentação (CS) está explicitamente presente no resumo: 'The CS technique, with a very large effect size, is the most effective among the three techniques.'

items.title: Does explaining the origins of misinformation improve the effectiveness of a given correction?

judge.evidence_topic: Misinformation often has a continuing influence on event-related reasoning even when it is clearly and credibly corrected; this is referred to as the continued influence effect.
judge.evidence_empirical: In two experiments, we examined whether a correction that explained misinformation as originating either from intentional deception or an unintentional error was more effective than a correction that only identified the misinformation as false.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) utilizando experimentos com cenários neutros (incêndio em armazém), atendendo aos critérios de neutralidade e método. O achado extraído reflete com precisão a conclusão do resumo de que explicar a origem da desinformação não aumenta a eficácia da correção.

items.title: Relative source credibility affects the continued influence effect: Evidence of rationality in the CIE

judge.evidence_topic: Participants read a fictitious news report in which original information and a retraction were each presented by either a source with high credibility or a source with low credibility.
judge.evidence_empirical: In two experiments ( N = 151, N = 146), informant credibility and retractor credibility were independently manipulated.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) utilizando cenários fictícios neutros, cumprindo os critérios de tópico e exclusão. O estudo é empírico (dois experimentos) e o método descrito condiz com o resumo. O achado principal é sustentado pelo texto do resumo.

items.title: Mechanisms in continued influence: The impact of misinformation corrections on source perceptions

judge.evidence_topic: Research on the continued influence effect (CIE) of misinformation has demonstrated that misinformation continues to influence people’s beliefs and judgments even after it has been corrected.
judge.evidence_empirical: Study 1 demonstrated that an external correction (i.e., a new source labeling misinformation as false) influences perceptions of the misinformation source... Study 2 replicated the results of Study 1... Study 3 was a preregistered replication of previous results using new methodology.
judge.reason: O artigo descreve três estudos experimentais com participantes humanos que investigam o efeito de influência continuada (CIE), alinhando-se ao pedido. O achado principal sobre a percepção da fonte como mecanismo de crença é sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: I know It's false, but I keep thinking as if it were true: A replication study of Johnson and Seifert's (1994) continued influence effect

judge.evidence_topic: The present research investigated the direct replicability of their study with a French-speaking sample, comparing the inferences drawn by an FI group (n = 21) to those made by a control group (n = 23).
judge.evidence_empirical: The present research investigated the direct replicability of their study with a French-speaking sample, comparing the inferences drawn by an FI group (n = 21) to those made by a control group (n = 23).
judge.reason: O artigo é uma replicação experimental direta do paradigma de Johnson e Seifert (1994), que utiliza cenários neutros (incêndio em armazém), atendendo aos critérios de neutralidade e método. Os dados extraídos estão corretos e sustentados pelo resumo.

items.title: Failure to accept retractions: A contribution to the continued influence effect

judge.evidence_topic: Previous research has shown that when information about a narrative event is retracted, people continue to use that information even though it has been explicitly identified as incorrect.
judge.evidence_empirical: Experiment 1 assessed this using a continued influence effect paradigm with an additional probe asking whether participants believed the explicitly stated change. Experiment 2 included an additional explicit instruction... Experiment 3 modified the alternative account to increase plausibility
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) em cenários narrativos neutros, utilizando experimentos com participantes humanos, o que está em conformidade com o pedido. O resumo não menciona temas proibidos (política, saúde, vacinas, COVID-19). O método descrito (experimentos com histórias narrativas) é condizente com o resumo. O achado principal é sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: Working memory capacity, short-term memory capacity, and the continued influence effect: A latent-variable analysis

judge.evidence_topic: Misinformation often affects inferences and judgments even after it has been retracted and discredited. This is known as the continued influence effect.
judge.evidence_empirical: Participants (N = 216) completed a continued-influence task, as well as a battery of WM and STM capacity tasks.
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico experimental sobre o efeito de influência continuada (CIE), publicado em 2018. O resumo confirma a amostra de 216 participantes e o achado principal de que a capacidade de memória de trabalho prediz a suscetibilidade ao efeito, enquanto a memória de curto prazo não. O tema é neutro e não envolve política, saúde ou vacinas.

items.title: Comparing the use of open and closed questions for Web-based measures of the continued-influence effect

judge.evidence_topic: We compared the data quality obtained using open and closed response formats using the continued-influence effect (CIE), in which participants read a series of statements about an unfolding event, one of which is unambiguously corrected later.
judge.evidence_empirical: We implemented this basic procedure online (Exp. 1A, n = 78), comparing standard open-ended responses to an alternative procedure using closed-ended responses (Exp. 1B, n = 75). Finally, we replicated these findings in a larger preregistered study (Exps. 2A and 2B, n = 323).
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) utilizando cenários fictícios neutros (eventos em desdobramento) e conduz experimentos empíricos com participantes humanos, atendendo a todos os critérios do pedido.

items.title: Does evaluating belief prior to its retraction influence the efficacy of later corrections?

items.title: Sensitivity to misinformation retractions in the continued influence paradigm: Evidence for stability

judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico experimental que investiga o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) utilizando tarefas padrão, o que se alinha ao recorte de neutralidade solicitado. items.title: Cause typicality and the continued influence effect

judge.evidence_topic: A large body of research has focused on whether and how readers update their knowledge of events when an initial piece of causal information is corrected. These studies have indicated that corrections can reduce, but do not eliminate, readers' reliance on the initial cause when drawing inferences or making decisions about the events (i.e., the continued influence effect).
judge.evidence_empirical: In three experiments, we interrogated the importance of cause typicality for the generalizable utility of these correction strategies by manipulating the typicality of initial and alternative causes.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) através de experimentos com participantes humanos utilizando cenários de eventos neutros. O método descrito no resumo condiz com o que foi extraído, e o achado principal é uma paráfrase direta do que está escrito no resumo.
